To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency was high in our sample of HIV-infected patients and that low vitamin D levels were associated with increased production of IFNγ and IL10 by peripheral blood monocytes and lymphocytes.

vitamin D status modulates the production of the proinflammatory Th1 cytokine, IFN-γ, and the antiinflammatory Th2 cytokine, IL-10, by PBMC in vitro, with a shift toward Th1 cytokine production at higher vitamin D levels and toward Th2 cytokine production at lower vitamin D levels.

vitamin D deficiency was associated with a decreased ability of PBMCs to produce the pro-inflammatory cytokine IFNgamma and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 in response to mitogen stimulation, while supplementation with vitamin D increased the production of these cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of vitamin D deficiency on immune response.
the study of the effects of vitamin D on the immune system, in particular, on the production of cytokines by PBMC in culture.
understanding how the immune system is affected by vitamin D status and how vitamin D may modulate cytokine responses to microbial stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vitamin D status is associated with the immune system, and that this association can be explained by the effects of vitamin D on immune cells.
vitamin D status has a modulatory effect on IFN-gamma and IL-10 production by PBMCs in culture, and this effect is influenced by vitamin D receptor polymorphisms.
there is no evidence that vitamin D deficiency causes MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vitamin D status modulates the cytokine profile of peripheral blood mononucleocytes.
vitamin D status has been found to have a significant effect on the production of interferon gamma and IL-10 in peripheral blood mononucleocytes.
the findings from the current study suggest a possible role for vitamin D in the modulation of immune function in children with asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that vitamin D is a key regulator of the immune response.
the vitamin D receptor is important in regulating T cell function, and this is a mechanism through which vitamin D can affect autoimmune diseases.
